messages:
jessie: Pager triggered: billing-counts.alert (token_count_delta > 3σ in 1m) for multiple customers — seeing oscillation between shadow and live counts. https://monitoring.redwood.ai/alerts/ABCD1234 :alarm_clock:

pagerbot: Incident created INC-2026-042, severity=P2. Oncall: @omar. Runbook: /runbooks/metering/count-drift. Paging schedule sent.

omar: I'm on it, grabbing logs + traces. @liam can you check whether any customer invoices were queued or emitted?

liam: Quick check — usage-report pipeline shows lag in eu-west-1 emitter. No invoices finalized yet, but two accounts got transient overage flags in staging (acct_842, acct_901). Investigating whether alerts were propagated to customers.

jessie: Noted. Let's avoid customer-facing notifications until we verify. Can we suppress overage alerting for the accounts while we triage? Playbook suggests a temporary suppression toggle.

eva: Suggest toggling emit-source -> shadow for the aggregate emitter to isolate live counting. Risk: short undercount for the current billing window but prevents false overage notifications. Recommend suppression + shadow toggle + backfill.

omar: Running diagnostics now: `ps aux | grep emitter` and `curl -s https://kafka-eu/status | jq .lag` -> lag=120000. Looks like consumer backpressure.

omar: Increasing consumer parallelism and restarting emitter-processor-2: `kubectl -n metering rollout restart deployment/emitter-processor-2`

jessie: Good. @liam please start a short customer comms draft for acct_842 and acct_901 (internal queue) in case we need to follow up. Keep wording conservative.

liam: Draft: "We're investigating an internal metering anomaly that may have temporarily flagged overages. No charges have been finalized; we've paused alerts and will confirm details by EOD." Will post once approved.

eva: Actioned: toggled emit-source=shadow at t=1812346040. Monitoring live vs shadow counts for divergence.

pagerbot: Alert updates: suppressed overage notifications for acct_842, acct_901 per incident INC-2026-042.

omar: Consumer lag improving — now 14k and trending down after scaling. Restart completed for emitter-processor-2, keeping watch for 10m.

jessie: Assigning postmortem owner: @eva. Please capture timeline, root-cause hypotheses, and rollback/tradeoff notes (why we chose shadow-mode + suppression). Incident doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/incidents/1812345999

liam: Re-checking billing queues: no invoices emitted, backfill queued. I'll run manual reconciliation once counts stabilize (will run `python tools/reconcile_counts.py --window 2026-03-17T10:00Z`).

omar: Snippet from emitter-processor-2 stderr during the burst: `CheckpointDelay: 2.1s; processed_batch=349; consumer_lag=120000` — looks like occasional GC + network hiccup exacerbated by load.

jessie: Great work. Keep monitoring for another 20m. Close when backfill completes and customer messages (if needed) are sent. :thumbsup:

eva: Noting mitigation tradeoff in the doc: temporary shadow-mode prevents false positives at the cost of more complex backfill. Will include verification checklist and follow-up tasks.

liam: I'll queue the customer messages after reconciliation; leaving placeholder in the incident doc.

jessie: Thanks team — update when backfill finishes.
